Hi Alice —

Thanks again for your time on today’s demo. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the performance targets you mentioned and outline the SLO checklist + proposed next steps (MAP items) so we’re aligned for procurement and the POC. Attached is a filled SLO checklist and the demo recording for the team.

Key items you called out during the demo:
- 99th percentile latency target: <= 350ms for short generation flows (~<256 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~250 requests/sec during peak business hours
- Concurrent active sessions: up to 50 concurrent streaming sessions (partial token streaming required)
- Token / request size: avg 120 tokens in, 220 tokens out (burst up to 1024)
- Availability target: 99.9% during business hours

Proposed next steps (MAP items):
1) POC environment spec + instance sizing (Redwood to provide sizing estimate) — due 6/25
2) 2-week canary with production traffic sampling + monitoring hooks — scope & metrics to agree 6/26
3) Security/compliance checklist exchange (SOC2 artifacts) — FinTechCo to confirm required docs
4) Commercial terms draft & procurement point-of-contact — FinTechCo to share procurement contact

Can you confirm the SLO targets above and whether anything else should be added to the MAP? If that looks good I’ll loop in Rishi + Logan to produce the instance-sizing spreadsheet and a canary rollout plan.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the recording — very helpful. Confirming the targets you captured with two clarifications:
- Throughput: 250 req/s sustained is our target for the auth+scoring path; there are several endpoints with heavier payloads but they are <10% of traffic.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for the UX (we show partial results to users). 50 concurrent streaming sessions is the 95th percentile; please size for 75 concurrent to allow headroom.

A couple of ask items from our side:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports partial-response streaming over websockets or only server-sent events? We prefer websockets for our front end.
- For the POC, we’ll want a simple dashboard with 99/95/90 latency percentiles and token-level cost visibility.

Procurement: looping in Mike (cc) who will handle contract + PO.

If you can update the MAP items to size for 75 concurrent streaming sessions and call out websocket support, we can move to a POC kickoff next week.

—Alice

Alice —

Appreciate the clarifications. Quick answers inline below and next actions: 

> Can you confirm whether Redwood supports partial-response streaming over websockets or only server-sent events?
Yes — Redwood supports both websocket-based streaming and server-sent events (SSE). For the POC we can enable websocket streaming end-to-end; Logan will share a short example snippet for the frontend integration.

> Size for 75 concurrent streaming sessions
Will do — we’ll size the POC for 75 concurrent streaming sessions (95th pct headroom) and include a 25% buffer for burst scenarios.

POC / MAP items (updated):
- Instance sizing + deployment topology (Redwood to deliver a spreadsheet with GPU types and expected RPS/latency) — deliverable: deployment-size-estimates.csv — owner: Rishi — due EOD 6/25

- Websocket streaming sample + integration notes — owner: Logan — due 6/25

- Commercial draft/term sheet — owner: Marissa (coordinate with Mike) — target 6/29

I’ve attached an updated SLO checklist with the concurrency change. Rishi — can you confirm GPU recommendations + expected throughput per instance in the next message? Logan — can you prepare the websocket example and canary metric template?

Thanks — will keep Aditya in the loop for any approvals on larger commitments.

Best,
Marissa

Following up with the sizing numbers and feasibility notes. Attachment: deployment-size-estimates.csv

Summary (ballpark):
- For 250 req/s sustained + 75 concurrent streaming sessions and your token profile (avg 120 in / 220 out):
  • Option A (single-model high perf): 4 x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent) in a cluster with autoscaling for burst — expected steady throughput ~300 req/s with 99th pct ~250-350ms depending on prompt complexity and batching window.
  • Option B (split routing + smaller GPUs): 6 x A10/NVidia q4_0 quantized variants with smart routing to a higher-capacity model on fallback — good cost tradeoff, slightly higher tail latency but lower unit cost.

- Streaming: websocket streaming supported end-to-end. Streaming adds CPU/IO overhead per connection — we recommend a separate gateway pool sized for concurrent connections (estimate: 75 concurrent sessions requires ~2 medium CPU gateway nodes with connection multiplexing).

- Batching & KV cache: enable continuous batching for short requests and prefix KV cache for repeated user prompts; this should reduce tail latency and token cost by ~15-25% in our tests.

- Canary + monitoring hooks: will expose latency percentiles, token counts, cost per token, streaming success rate, and a health endpoint for the gateway to track connection churn.

Next steps: I’ll finalize the CSV with exact instance types and expected RPS per instance. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min sizing review tomorrow.

—Rishi
